clauses.reason: Keep generic mechanisms separate from repository-specific facts and approval.

updates.rationale: Nesting repository gates duplicates retries, receipts, cleanup and eligibility rules.
updates.statement: A declared repository provider supplies structured selection through one validated boundary; the existing generic runner and evidence owner execute and judge it.

updates.rationale: A working-set table can be authority without being a decision log, and missing provenance must not be invented.
scope: Historical authority inventory and migration preview
updates.statement: Historical working sets enter inventory only through explicit committed source declarations; mappings preserve source facts and remain unapproved until separately accepted.

decisions.reason: The owner authorized the Signetum side of the reviewed Perdura adoption plan.

boundaries: A provider never owns a second gate or receipt.
Discovery and mapping previews never confer approval.
revision.summary: Repositories supply selection and historical source facts; Signetum owns validation and review mechanisms.

observations.reason: Preserve the single writer identity boundary; correct the candidate identities before any application.
observations.summary: Initial proposal identities were not prefixed by their owning change; the writer refused the request without changing source.

transaction.reason: Apply the exact owner-approved standalone boundary decision before implementation.

resolutions.reason: Only candidate identity namespace changed; approved outcomes and source authority remain the same.

observations.reason: Preserve prohibition, basis, reopen conditions and remaining unmapped rows; opt-in inventories use schema version two while undeclared repositories keep the old CLI shape.
observations.summary: Declared Markdown constraint sources need their own inventory status and exact row accounting, rather than being parsed as accepted decision documents.

transaction.reason: Retain the explicit adoption boundary before freezing its source.
Bind the implemented row-preserving source boundary to its committed behavioral evidence.

resolutions.reason: Engine, generated and isolated public frontends retain exact rows and source identity and refuse bad bindings, stale previews and weakened mappings; 94 migration/manifest cases pass.

observations.reason: Four engine/generated public-boundary cases reproduced these omissions. Target identity must bind the actual file argument; modified files require whole-file execution or the full declared shard.
observations.summary: A producer could claim file A while its argv selected file B, or name only one node of a modified test file.

transaction.reason: Retain reproduced selection-proof gaps before freezing the source.

observations.reason: Provider code, rules, tools and exact response proof must remain bound through readiness and admission. An open merge has no committed provider source and therefore uses full declared member diagnostics; unsupported target conventions retain whole-shard selection.
observations.summary: Selection declarations remain below evidence types; typed request values are layered above the manifest to avoid an import cycle. The producer narrows only a declared file-target tail, not the runner or final gate.

transaction.reason: Keep the execution boundary and conservative exceptional-state behavior explicit before freezing source.
Bind reproduced selection boundaries to the committed implementation and public behavioral evidence.

resolutions.reason: Arguments bind exact regular test files or their nodes; every modified test file executes whole or through its full shard. Reproduced omitted-file and narrowed-modified-file cases now refuse in both frontends.

Typed provider contexts, artifact/tool binding, exact proof recheck, safe inheritance and full final commands are exercised through real members. Open-merge checks fail on an unselected full-suite defect, preserve the merge, and continue only after repair; installed exported runtime also executes selection and working-set inventory.

observations.reason: Only actual supported top-level tables may supply rows; examples stay context and unsupported constraint tables need explicit review diagnostics. Preserve the interrupted readiness and red reproductions rather than crediting earlier successful tests.
observations.summary: A shorter closing marker could end a longer code fence, indented examples could supply constraint rows, and unsupported multi-column headers could be silently ignored.

transaction.reason: Final source review found examples being treated as rules; the in-flight readiness was intentionally interrupted without a success claim.
Bind the source-framing repair to committed public inventory reproductions.

resolutions.reason: Fence marker and minimum length now govern closing; indented code cannot open a table; unsupported constraint columns produce a review issue. Six engine/generated reproductions preserve actual rules before and after examples; all 92 migration cases pass and the real working-set format still yields 135 rows without ambiguity. The interrupted readiness is not successful evidence.

observations.reason: Two engine/generated real-member reproductions fail. Full declared tree-shard coverage remains valid without file refinement; exact whole-file proof remains mandatory only when a target list narrows that shard.
observations.summary: A provider selecting an unchanged full tree shard was required to declare a file-target refinement binding, even though no command was narrowed.

transaction.reason: A documented no-refinement mode was refused by the modified-test proof and requires a correction before readiness.
Bind the no-refinement correction to real member and admission evidence.

resolutions.reason: An unchanged declared tree shard can cover a modified test without a file-target binding. Narrowed commands still require exact whole-file proof. Both engine and generated members become ready and are admitted through full commands; all 48 selection scenarios pass.
